subject: [PATCH v8 5/8] fuse: {io-uring} Allow reduced queues through INIT negotiation

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Bernd Schubert questioned the necessity of using ADD_QUEUE for this feature, pointing out that he had previously held back updates on the series until ADD_QUEUE was implemented in kernel and libfuse, and expressing concern about the performance implications of adding a queue and then waiting for an entry.

Reviewer noted that the consolidated mapping logic should handle both legacy and dynamic paths, including older libfuse cases, to avoid special casing.
reviews.raw_body:
Why do we need ADD_QUEUE for this feature then? Didn't you especially
ask to use ADD_QUEUE for dynamic queues? I was basically holding back
any updates on this series until ADD_QUEUE was implemented in kernel and
libfuse and now we go the other way around. Without the request to do it
through ADD_QUEUE this series would have been ready a few months back...

Personally I see that the current way makes registering new queues
rather expensive from fuse-server, because we first add a queue and then
need to wait for the entry, which

a) either adds delays in request handling
b) or make libfuse complex, because it needs to link SQEs

---

Yeah, I was thinking about this as well. Though we need to handle both
cases for older libfuse - there will be special cases one way or the other.


Thanks,
Bernd

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged reviewer's suggestion to consolidate mapping logic and agreed to restructure the code in a future version, but clarified that the ADD_QUEUE part would remain unchanged.

Author pushed back on reviewer's suggestion to consolidate mapping logic, arguing that servers wanting advanced io-uring features already need to use ADD_QUEUE and therefore reduced queues should not be added to the legacy interface.
reviews.raw_body:
The consolidated path wouldn't drop ADD_QUEUE, that part would stay
exactly as it is (eg it creates the queue with its config (zero copy,
bufpool needs the queue to exist, etc.) and REGISTER still requires it
in reduced mode. The only part that gets changed / consolidated is how
the mappings get set.

Feel free to defer this. I can send out a patch for this after your
series lands, if that makes things easier.

---

Any servers that want advanced io-uring features (zero copy, bufpools)
will already need to go through ADD_QUEUE. imo it doesn't make sense
to also add compatibility for reduced queues to the legacy interface.

Thanks,
Joanne

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch consolidates the logic for creating and updating the mapping of queues to CPU IDs in the FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace) implementation of io-uring. The current approach has two separate flows for legacy and dynamic queue paths, which are merged into a single flow. In this new flow, the mapping is updated on the first registration of a queue, and it's built from the global registered queue mask. This change also fixes an issue where requests mapped to a queue could get lost if there was a failure between adding the queue and registering its first entry. Additionally, the patch allows dynamic queues to be advertised, which enables rejecting qids that don't map to possible CPU IDs during ADD_QUEUE.
